# Learn to Upholster — The Working Upholsterer's Bible

> The complete text of The Working Upholsterer's Bible by Shaun Greenwood (master upholsterer, AMUSF accredited, Greenwood Upholstery, Hebden Bridge), published free online. Traditional and modern upholstery: materials, techniques, full step-by-step projects, business guidance for working upholsterers, and free calculators.

The complete text in one file: https://www.learntoupholster.com/llms-full.txt
Queryable over MCP, including six upholstery calculators: https://www.learntoupholster.com/mcp (documentation: https://www.learntoupholster.com/use-in-ai)

## Chapters and pages

- [A Brief, Opinionated History of Upholstery](https://www.learntoupholster.com/a-brief-opinionated-history-of-upholstery): A brief, opinionated history of upholstery — from mediaeval cushions and Tudor state beds to Pratt’s coil spring, the staple gun, and today’s craft revival.
- [A customer hasn't collected their furniture](https://www.learntoupholster.com/business/uncollected-furniture): Chase it in writing early, and have terms that let you charge storage. Finished furniture sitting in a workshop is money you have already spent and space…
- [About](https://www.learntoupholster.com/about): Learn to Upholster is a free upholstery reference and companion to the book The Working Upholsterer's Bible, by master upholsterer Shaun Greenwood.
- [Australia & New Zealand Upholstery Fire Regulations](https://www.learntoupholster.com/fire-regulations-australia-new-zealand): The AS/NZS upholstery flammability standards are voluntary. There is no mandatory domestic requirement in either country.
- [A–Z glossary of upholstery terms](https://www.learntoupholster.com/a-z-glossary): An A-Z of around 150 upholstery terms, from antimacassar to zigzag spring, in plain English and cross-referenced to the relevant chapters.
- [Box Cushion Fabric & Cutting Calculator](https://www.learntoupholster.com/box-cushion-calculator): Free box cushion calculator: enter width, depth and height for a full cutting list, boxing, zip border and piping, in metric and imperial.
- [Business Hub — free resources for working upholsterers](https://www.learntoupholster.com/business/): Free business resources for working upholsterers: pricing, quoting, finding customers, running a workshop and making a living from the craft.
- [Buy the Book: Wiro-Bound Workshop Edition](https://www.learntoupholster.com/buy-the-book): The wiro-bound A4 workshop edition of The Working Upholsterer's Bible: 35 chapters, 72 figures, lies flat on the bench. Printed to order in the UK.
- [Can you make a living from upholstery?](https://www.learntoupholster.com/business/can-you-make-a-living-from-upholstery): Yes, but almost certainly not in the way you are picturing. Very few people make a living from one kind of upholstery.
- [Canada upholstery fire regulations](https://www.learntoupholster.com/fire-regulations-canada): No flammability standard for upholstered furniture. All three provincial schemes were repealed between 2019 and 2021.
- [Caravan and holiday park work](https://www.learntoupholster.com/business/caravan-and-holiday-park-work): It is maintenance, not upholstery in the way most of us mean the word. Holiday parks want their existing furniture kept in service as long as possible —…
- [Chair Frame Repair & Joint Reinforcement](https://www.learntoupholster.com/frame-repair-and-joint-reinforcement): The frame repairs every upholsterer should handle: re-gluing loose mortise-and-tenon joints with hide glue, splicing a worn-out tacking rail, and treating.
- [Chesterfield Sofa: Deep-Buttoned Leather Restoration](https://www.learntoupholster.com/chesterfield-sofa): The Chesterfield restoration end to end: the form, materials, button counts by size, deep buttoning in leather, dampening pleats, brass-nail trim at 25 mm.
- [Choosing the Right Upholstery Fabric: A Beginner's Guide](https://www.learntoupholster.com/choosing-the-right-fabric): How to choose upholstery fabric: reading a fabric label, the eight fibre families, Martindale and Wyzenbeek rub ratings and which band you need, pattern.
- [Contact](https://www.learntoupholster.com/contact): Get in touch with Learn to Upholster — questions about the site, the book or the tools. Email shaun@greenwoodupholstery.com.
- [Contents — Learn to Upholster](https://www.learntoupholster.com/contents): The full contents of The Working Upholsterer's Bible — foundations, techniques, complete projects, the working workshop, and reference. Free to read.
- [Customer's own fabric](https://www.learntoupholster.com/business/customer-supplied-fabric): You can, but set the terms in writing first. You cannot guarantee cloth you did not source, you lose the fabric margin that forms part of a job's profit…
- [Customers & the Upholstery Workshop Year](https://www.learntoupholster.com/customers-and-the-workshop-year): The business side of upholstery: the first customer conversation, managing expectations, quoting with confidence, and the seasonal rhythm of the year.
- [Deep Buttoning & Tufting: The Diamond Grid Explained](https://www.learntoupholster.com/buttoning-and-tufting): Deep buttoning and tufting explained: setting out the diamond grid, pulling buttons through to a backing patch, and forming the diagonal pleats cleanly.
- [Deep-Buttoning & Diamond Calculator](https://www.learntoupholster.com/deep-buttoning-calculator): A free deep-buttoning calculator for upholsterers: work out the diamond button layout and count, the base and fabric marking grids, the fabric fullness.
- [Do you need formal training to become an upholsterer?](https://www.learntoupholster.com/blog/do-you-need-training-to-be-an-upholsterer): Legally, no — upholstery is unregulated and anyone can trade tomorrow. What training actually buys you, what it does not, and the obligations that apply whether you trained or not.
- [Drop-In Dining Seat: A Complete Beginner's Project](https://www.learntoupholster.com/drop-in-dining-seat): How to reupholster a drop-in dining chair seat, step by step: stripping, webbing, stuffing, the top cover and the bottoming cloth.
- [Explaining why upholstery costs what it does](https://www.learntoupholster.com/business/explaining-what-upholstery-costs): Do not justify it — explain what they are buying. A new sofa at the same price is a different product: a stapled softwood frame with a five-year life…
- [Find an Upholsterer Near You: UK, US & Worldwide](https://www.learntoupholster.com/find-an-upholsterer): How to find a good upholsterer near you: search the vetted AMUSF member directory in the UK, find local upholsterers on the map anywhere, and the questions.
- [Fitting the Top Cover: Calico, Wadding & Corner Pleats](https://www.learntoupholster.com/calico-wadding-and-top-cover): Fitting an upholstery cover properly: the calico under-cover as a dress rehearsal, the wadding that smooths it, then cutting and fitting the show fabric.
- [Fluted Chair in Blue — Upholstery Project](https://www.learntoupholster.com/projects/fluted-chair): A modern fluted-back chair covered in three clean movements: the arms, the inside back and the outside back. A study in economy on the bench.
- [Foam & Cushion Density Calculator by Project](https://www.learntoupholster.com/foam-cushion-calculator): A free foam selector for upholstery: pick the application and get the right foam type, density, firmness, depth, Dacron wrap and fire grade (CMHR / Crib 5).
- [Foam Cushion Construction: Cutting, Bonding & Dacron](https://www.learntoupholster.com/foam-construction): Modern foam upholstery, step by step: the two-foam principle (HD base plus soft top), choosing foam by density, cutting with a serrated knife, spray-bonding.
- [Free Fabric Visualiser: See Your Chair in Your Fabric](https://www.learntoupholster.com/fabric-visualiser): See your chair or sofa in a different fabric: upload the piece and a swatch, and preview it re-covered in seconds, free, with tips for a realistic result.
- [Free Printable Upholstery Workshop Forms](https://www.learntoupholster.com/workshop-forms): Four free printable forms for an upholstery workshop: customer enquiry, condition report, job sheet, and delivery note. No download, no account.
- [Free Upholstery Invoice & Quote Template (Excel)](https://www.learntoupholster.com/invoice-template): A free quote, order form and invoice template for upholstery businesses: deposit terms, customer's-own-material lines, fire-safety wording and a VAT toggle.
- [Getting your first customers](https://www.learntoupholster.com/business/getting-your-first-customers): Start with the people who already send work to upholsterers rather than with the public.
- [How do you clean a fabric sofa?](https://www.learntoupholster.com/blog/how-to-clean-a-fabric-sofa): Read the cleaning code, vacuum first, blot instead of scrub, use little liquid, and dry at room temperature. Stop before you leave a ring.
- [How much should an upholsterer charge?](https://www.learntoupholster.com/business/how-much-should-an-upholsterer-charge): Build it up from your own costs rather than copying a competitor. Take your annual overheads, add the wage you need, add a margin for tax and…
- [How to look after a leather sofa](https://www.learntoupholster.com/blog/how-to-look-after-a-leather-sofa): Which finish you have decides everything, and there is a two-minute test that tells you. The routine that keeps leather alive for decades, and the everyday products that quietly destroy it.
- [How to Strip a Chair for Reupholstery](https://www.learntoupholster.com/stripping-the-old-work): How to strip an old chair for reupholstering: working outside-in, reading the tack holes in the old timber, what to save and what to bin, and the three-part.
- [I don't want this job — how do I say no?](https://www.learntoupholster.com/business/saying-no-to-a-job): Decline quickly, politely, and without a detailed justification. "I'm afraid it's not something I can take on" is a complete sentence and needs no…
- [I'm busy but I'm not making money](https://www.learntoupholster.com/business/busy-but-not-making-money): Almost always because your hourly rate is set from what you hope customers will pay rather than what the workshop costs to run.
- [Identifying British Chair & Sofa Styles by Period](https://www.learntoupholster.com/historical-style-guide): A quick-lookup reference to the named chair and sofa forms most common in British upholstery — Georgian, Victorian and Howard wing-backs, Chesterfield.
- [Industrial sewing for upholsterers](https://www.learntoupholster.com/sewing): Industrial sewing for upholsterers: thread, needles, machines and troubleshooting, explained from an upholstery bench rather than a sail loft.
- [Industrial Sewing Machines for Upholstery](https://www.learntoupholster.com/sewing-machines): Industrial sewing machines for upholstery: drop, needle, walking foot and compound feed explained, plus flat, cylinder, post and long arm beds.
- [Insurance for an upholstery workshop](https://www.learntoupholster.com/business/insurance-for-an-upholstery-workshop): More than most workshops carry, and in a different shape than they expect. Public liability is the one everybody buys — but it usually excludes damage to…
- [Ireland upholstery fire regulations](https://www.learntoupholster.com/fire-regulations-ireland): Its own 1995 Order and Irish Standard, close to the British regime but a separate legal instrument.
- [Is bonded leather worth repairing?](https://www.learntoupholster.com/blog/is-bonded-leather-worth-repairing): No. Kits and recoats will not hold on a surface that is still coming apart. Tell bonded from real leather, then decide recover or replace from the frame.
- [Is it cheaper to reupholster or buy new?](https://www.learntoupholster.com/blog/is-it-cheaper-to-reupholster-or-buy-new): Usually not, if you compare it to the cheapest new sofa in the sale — but that is the wrong comparison. What actually decides it is the frame, and how to check yours in two minutes.

- [Why does leather peel?](https://www.learntoupholster.com/blog/why-does-leather-peel): Real leather does not peel. What peels is bonded leather or a polyurethane coating — how to tell which you have, why it fails, and what can actually be repaired.
- [Why does velvet go patchy?](https://www.learntoupholster.com/blog/why-does-velvet-go-patchy): Velvet does not go patchy — it shades. Why pile fabric changes colour as it is pressed, which velvets recover and which mark permanently, and what pile direction does to your fabric quantity.
- [Why has my sofa gone saggy in the middle?](https://www.learntoupholster.com/blog/why-has-my-sofa-gone-saggy): Something under the cushions has failed, and it is usually not the cushions. How to tell whether it is the foam, the webbing, the springs or the frame — and which of those is worth fixing.
- [Why is my sofa fabric bobbling?](https://www.learntoupholster.com/blog/why-is-my-sofa-fabric-bobbling): Pilling is loose fibre working to the surface, and it is usually not a fault. Why blends pill worst, why it normally stops on its own, and the separate test standard nobody tells you to ask about.
